pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
DEPTH PERCEPTION

Sandbox Software, Pittsburgh. 3:00 in the morning.

The render of the century is crawling down the monitor one scan line at a time: the box art for Depth Perception, a perfect checkerboard running to the horizon, chrome spheres, a glass cube, a red teapot and the morning sun coming up behind them all. It has been rendering for eleven hours. It is 99% done. Everybody went home. Doc Leo, our lighting director, left his spotlight on.

Then COUNT POLYGON crept in through the modem.

The Count lives on polygons. He took the gold sphere's and left it an icosahedron. He took the teapot's and left it a brick. He spread his henchmen through every scene of the render: wireframes that were never finished, jaggies made of nothing but stair steps, and polygon bats.

He missed one. RAY, the chrome sphere from every ray tracing demo ever made, still has every polygon he was born with. Roll him through six scenes, collect the red, green and blue lenses, and get him to each scene's vanishing point, where all the parallel lines meet. The box art goes to the printer at nine.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type DEPTH and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker beeps along. Every picture in the game was rendered ahead of time, so a 386 plays it as well as a 486.

From the menu, pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute to watch a demonstration. Read Storyline shows how the night went wrong; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

Light and lives

Ray runs on light. He starts with 100 and three lives. Henchmen, steam and bats cost light; light bulbs, friends and THE CHEZ's charge port give it back. Fall into the void and the render of Ray simply falls apart: you start that scene over, with every lens you have found still in your pocket. Press F2 to see your score, light and lives.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W S A D		Roll. Ray stops when you let go - he's a very well-behaved sphere.
Q E
keypad 7 9 1 3		Roll diagonally: Q up-left, E up-right; the number pad corners go all four ways.
SpaceFire a ray of light the way you last rolled. It renders a wireframe into a crystal (touch the crystal for points) and takes faces off Count Polygon.
F1-F6Help, status, music on/off, sound on/off, save, load.
EscQuit to the menu.

A joystick works too: push to roll, button 1 fires.

pages.head: Pulling Focus
pages.html:
Pulling Focus

Every scene in the render has two planes: the near plane and the far plane. A camera can only focus on one at a time, and in Depth Perception that is the whole trick:

Sharp things are solid. A blur isn't there.

Near blocks are amber; far blocks are cyan. When the near plane is in focus, amber blocks are crisp and solid and cyan ones are soft, see-through blurs you can roll right through. Pull focus to the far plane and it's the other way round.

Focus rings

Roll onto a focus ring (a chrome ring set in the floor) to pull focus to the other plane. The lens inside the ring glows the color of where it will take you. Ray's own bands tell you which plane is in focus: amber near, cyan far.

Glass walkways

Glass walkways are only there in their own plane: an amber walkway holds you up when the near plane is in focus and is just a blur over the void when it isn't. Violet auto-focus panels drift in and out of focus on their own; wait for them to sharpen, then roll. A panel flickers pink twice just before it blurs out, so a flicker means stay put.

A fresh render

Pulling focus re-renders the scene the way it was: photons and bulbs come back, and gates close again. The lenses you've found stay with you.

pages.head: Things in the Render
pages.html:
Things in the Render

PhotonA little star of light: 25 points.
Light bulb30 light in the first two scenes, 20 in the next two and 15 in the last two: the closer the render is to done, the scarcer light gets.
Red, green and blue lensesOne of each in every scene. The RGB gate before the vanishing point takes one of each.
RGB gateThree glass doors in a row: red, green, blue. Each opens only for its lens.
Vanishing pointThe white light at the end of each scene.
SlopesGolden chevrons in the Fractal Peaks pull you the way they point. Ride them down; don't ride them into a pit.
TeapotsThe Utah teapot, the most rendered object there is. In the Teapot Temple they puff steam at you.
THE CHEZA 1976 1/2 CitiCar, plugged in on the rear passenger side. Push against its charge port for light.

pages.head: Friends and Fiends
pages.html:
Friends and Fiends

Friends

Teddy, a Pembroke Welsh corgi with a big grin, strolls the Checkerboard. Gwinn, sitting pretty in her pink collar, keeps the Glass Garden. Doc Leo, our lighting director (fedora, green tie, red sneakers and a rubber chicken on a leash), paces the Teapot Temple. Bump into any of them for a little light. Henchmen that bump into them get rendered.

Fiends

WireframesNever finished. One ray renders them into crystals.
JaggiesAliasing with teeth. They hop along their beat.
Your dark doubleThe Hall of Mirrors' reflection that rolls at you when you get close.
SteamFrom the teapots. Hot.
Polygon batsThe Count's, from their nests at the vanishing point.
ShardsThrown by the four prisms in Count Polygon's arena. A prism glows pink just before it throws. Shards are slow and a ray shatters them.
COUNT POLYGONTwenty faces of vampire. He swoops round you and dives. A ray cracks him, a second shatters him, a third takes faces off: twenty, then eight. When the eight are gone he coughs up the blue lens he swallowed and flees into the far plane, where he waits with four faces, then a triangle, then a point. What he leaves behind opens the last door.

pages.head: The Six Scenes
pages.html:
The Six Scenes

1. The Checkerboard. Where every render begins. Learn to pull focus.

2. The Glass Garden. Crystals, glass tiles and auto-focus panels over the void.

3. The Hall of Mirrors. Nine rooms joined by near doors and far doors, around a middle room drawn isometrically, as if the camera had swung round to a corner. Which one of you is real?

4. Fractal Peaks. Infinitely detailed, mostly downhill. The plateau at the top is seen isometrically, amber blocks standing a tier taller than cyan.

5. Teapot Temple. A colonnade, three shrines, an isometric sanctum around the vanishing point and a parked CitiCar.

6. The Vanishing Point. Where all parallel lines meet, and Count Polygon waits in an arena drawn isometrically: amber near cubes stand a full tier tall, cyan far cubes half that. Beat him in the near plane, then follow him up through the blue gate into the far plane.

pages.head: Tips from the Render Farm
pages.html:
Tips from the Render Farm

  • Look before you roll: if a block is soft and see-through, it isn't there right now.
  • A focus ring always drops you off on its far side. Step back onto it to pull focus back.
  • A lens boxed in by blocks of one color is a puzzle, not a wall: find the ring that turns that color to a blur.
  • Fire before a wireframe reaches you: a rendered crystal is worth points; a bump costs light.
  • The auto-focus panels keep time. Count it while you wait on solid ground.
  • Lost a life? The scene starts over, but your lenses don't.
  • Count Polygon doesn't move until you come within reach. Pick your spot first, and keep a cube between you and the prisms.
  • He swoops to one side, then the other, then dives. Line up as he swings by, and roll clear when he dives.
  • Not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall.

printables.pitch: Roll a chrome sphere through six ray-traced worlds and pull focus between near and far: sharp is solid, a blur isn't there.

news.head: We threw away the cardboard glasses
news.html: Our art department spent a week squinting through red and blue cellophane before Doc Leo said what everybody was thinking: real depth isn't two colors, it's focus. Depth Perception has a near plane and a far plane in every scene, and only the one in focus is solid. The glasses are still in the box. You won't need them.

news.head: How long does a render take?
news.html: Every block, sprite and cartoon in Depth Perception was ray traced on our office 486. The intro alone took a long weekend. The box art took eleven hours and a vampire. We are told the next machine will be faster.

news.head: Since last issue: The Word Counter is still thinking
news.html: KEEP IT BRIEF! readers have put a lot of stories back together this month. The Word Counter found exactly one hundred words in each one but Steam-Powered Summer, where it found ninety-nine until somebody pointed out what a hyphen does. It is still thinking about it. Judging by the BBS, so are some of you.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Our lighting director
news.html: Doc Leo has a new title. He spent so many nights at the office watching renders crawl down the screen that we made him our lighting director, which mostly means he leaves the spotlight on. He paces the Teapot Temple with his rubber chicken, Teddy strolls the Checkerboard, Gwinn sits pretty in the Glass Garden and THE CHEZ is parked in the temple, charging. Gwinn's sit is ray traced. We're counting it.

news.head: In the workshop: We are getting around to it
news.html: Since our first disk you've asked for a role-playing game, and since our first disk we've said we'd get around to it. We're getting around to it: Quest for the Round Tuit, a whole kingdom where everything gets done, eventually. Towns, dungeons, a quest log, and a horseless carriage you may recognize.

news.head: Letters: "A corgi in my library book"
news.html:
"I found a corgi in one of the library books. Is that allowed?" - A reader, by mail

The Scoop replies: Teddy is allowed. Gwinn is not allowed in the library, and is in the library.

items.title: Depth Perception Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: From the render farm's log book. Lay the red film over an answer to read it - the only red glasses this game will ever ask you to wear.

hints.q: How do I get past a wall of amber blocks?
hints.a: Amber blocks are the near plane. Find a focus ring with a cyan lens and roll onto it: the far plane comes into focus and the amber blocks turn to blurs you can roll through.

hints.q: I pulled focus and now I'm stuck.
hints.a: Every focus ring works both ways. Step off it and back onto it to pull focus back. You arrive on the far side of the ring each time.

hints.q: Why did the photons come back?
hints.a: Pulling focus re-renders the scene the way it was. Photons, bulbs and gates come back; your lenses stay in your pocket.

hints.q: Where is the red lens?
hints.a: Behind the column of amber blocks. Pull focus at the ring left of the column and roll straight through.

hints.q: How do I cross the chasm?
hints.a: In the near plane the amber walkway holds you. Roll onto the ring in the middle: the far plane comes into focus and the cyan walkway takes you the rest of the way.

hints.q: The violet panels keep disappearing under me.
hints.a: They drift in and out of focus together, about two seconds each way. Wait on solid ground until they sharpen, then roll without stopping. A pink flicker means a panel is about to blur out: don't step on.

hints.q: The green lens is across three sets of panels.
hints.a: The middle set keeps the opposite time to the others. Cross one set, wait on the little island for the next to sharpen, and go again.

hints.q: Which doors can I use?
hints.a: Amber doors open in the far plane, cyan doors in the near plane. The ring in the middle room pulls focus.

hints.q: My double keeps rolling into me.
hints.a: It wakes when you come close. Face it and fire first: one ray renders it to nothing.

hints.q: The green lens is boxed in by cyan blocks.
hints.a: Cyan blocks are solid in the far plane, the only plane that gets you into that room. Roll onto the ring beside the box: in the near plane the box is a blur. Take the lens, then step back on the ring to get out.

hints.q: The arrows carried me away!
hints.a: Golden chevrons pull you the way they point until you hit something. Ride the two chutes on purpose; stay off the slopes beside the pit.

hints.q: The blue lens is boxed in by amber blocks.
hints.a: You cross the glass bridge in the near plane, where amber is solid. The ring in that room pulls focus to the far plane, where the box is a blur. Take the lens and ride the ring back.

hints.q: I'm low on light.
hints.a: THE CHEZ is plugged in at the parking lot. Stand below its rear wheel and push up against the charge port: it charges you, and keeps charging.

hints.q: The steam keeps getting me.
hints.a: A ray puts out a puff. Keep moving past the teapots rather than standing beside them.

hints.q: How do I beat Count Polygon?
hints.a: He waits until you come within reach, then swoops: to one side of you, to the other, then straight at you. Line up with him across or down the arena, turn to face him and fire. A ray cracks him, a second shatters him and a third takes faces off. When his eight faces are gone he coughs up the blue lens he swallowed and flees into the far plane: take the lens, roll through the blue gate at the top of the arena and finish him there.

hints.q: Purple shards keep hitting me.
hints.a: The four prisms in the arena throw them, a little faster in the far plane. A prism glows pink just before it throws. Shards are slow: roll away, put a cube between you, or shoot them.

hints.q: The last door won't open.
hints.a: It wants the last polygon the Count leaves behind in the far plane. Roll over it, then go through the gold door and the red and green gates.

hints.q: Somebody felted something into the render...
hints.a: Not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall. Look for a mirror with something faint inside it.

hints.q: I found a mirror I can roll through. Now what?
hints.a: Behind it is the Prism Egg on a pedestal. Roll onto it and press Enter to pick it up and keep it. Leave by the mirror just above the one you came in by.

hints.q: Just draw me a map.
hints.a: In the far plane, go up through the amber door into the top middle room, then right into the top right room past the red lens. Its right wall has two two-way mirrors; with the far plane in focus, roll through the lower one, then press Enter on the felt egg.
